title: Efficiency of protein-protein interactions in mammalian cells determined by a dual-light assay
protocol: Clone the deactivation/activation unit containing polyadenylation signal, DNA binding site, TATA box, splicing unit beginning and ending with exons and 5' UTR into the Sal I and Bam HI sites of pBPLUGA.
Generate a fluorescence reporter by cloning the D/A unit into the multiple cloning site of DsRedExpress-GFP vector.
Delete polyadenylation site, the splicing unit, and the 5' UTR to create a negative control construct.
Clone your gene of interest into the multiple cloning site of vectors pTN111 and pTN112 for bait and prey constructs.
Seed 2X 10^5 to 4X 10^5 HEK293 cells into each well of a 12-well plate.
Prepare plates in duplicate, one for fluorescence microscopy and one for preparing cell extract.
Grow the cells overnight in a humidified atmosphere at 37 °C and 5-10% CO₂.
Remove the plate from the incubator and examine it briefly under a microscope to ensure the cells are in good condition for transfection.
Add 30-50 ng of reporter plasmids (pTN114 and pTN124), 80-100 ng of bait and prey plasmids derived from pTN111 and pTN112 into a 0.5ml sterile tube.
Prepare samples in duplicate.
For negative control, prepare a tube with no plasmid DNA.
For reporter control, prepare a tube with only reporter plasmid (pTN114 or pTN124).
For bait control, prepare a tube with reporter and bait plasmids.
For prey control, prepare a tube with reporter and prey plasmids.
Prepare a transfection mixture by mixing 25 μl of serum-free medium and 2.5 μl Gene Jammer transfection reagent in a sterile tube.
Mix the reagent and medium either by pipetting or inverting the tube four to five times.
Incubate the mixture for 5-10 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the medium using an aspirator and examine under a microscope to ensure that the cells are not aspirated.
Pre-warm complete medium by placing it in a 37°C water bath for 10-15 minutes.
Add drop-wise the mixture onto each well and incubate for 3 hours in the incubator.
After 3 hours, add an additional 500 μl of pre-warmed medium into each well and incubate for 48 hours in the incubator.
Remove the plate from the incubator after 48 hours and examine the expression of green and red fluorescence proteins under a fluorescence microscope.
Discard the medium from each well forty-eight hours after transfection.
Add 200 μl TEN7.5 into each well.
Incubate the plate for 5-10 minutes at room temperature.
Gently pipette the solution up and down for 5-6 times to dissociate cells from the well, then transfer them into a new tube.
Spin down the cells at 1000 g in a bench-top cold centrifuge and discard the medium.
Add 100 μl 1 X Reporter Lysis Buffer into each tube.
Vortex the tube for 10 seconds or until a homogenous mixture is achieved.
Freeze the cells onto dry ice for 3-5 minutes.
Thaw the cells by incubating in a 37°C water bath for 2 minutes.
Repeat the freeze and thaw procedure one to two times.
Spin down the cells at 10000 g in a cold centrifuge.
Transfer supernatant into a pre-cooled 0.5 ml tube.
Store the tubes on ice.
Add 12.5 μl of Buffer A into a luminometer tube.
Add 2-10 μl of cell extracts to the tube.
Add 50 μl of Buffer B containing Galacton Plus and measure luciferase activity.
Incubate the sample for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Add 50 μl of Accelerator-II and measure beta-galactosidase activity.
Determine the activities in duplicate if using a tube luminometer.
Determine the activities in triplicate if using a plate luminometer.
Determine the ratio of luciferase and β-galactosidase activities.
Separate 20 μl of cell extracts and a pre-stained marker by SDS PAGE gel.
Transfer the proteins onto nitrocellulose membrane.
Block the membrane with 5% milk for one hour at room temperature.
Wash the membrane with TBS containing 0.1% Tween 20 for 5 minutes at room temperature on a rocking shaker.
Incubate the membrane with primary antibody at 4°C for overnight.
Wash the membrane with TBS containing 0.1% Tween 20 three to five times on a rocking shaker as described in step 31.
Incubate the membrane with secondary antibody at room temperature for 1 hour.
Wash the membrane with TBS containing 0.1% Tween 20 three to five times on a rocking shaker as mentioned in step 34.
Develop the membrane using ECL Western Blotting Detection Reagents.
